_about: Where to stay, base by base, from docs/research/07-lodging.md (researched 1 Oct 2026) and the plan doc's Where to sleep. Prices are JPY per night for the whole group of six, rounded; ryokan prices include dinner and breakfast. 'Verified' means read on an official site, Ikyu, Rakuten or a current guide; otherwise it is the sector pattern. Live availability for 31 Dec must be checked in a browser.

ground_rules.title: Decide the New Year anchor first
ground_rules.text: The three New Year nights (31 Dec–2 Jan) are the only scarce resource; everything else is still open. Most small ryokan load rooms six months out and their New Year plans sell out within weeks of posting in September. City hotels, apartment hotels and machiya do not have that cliff.

ground_rules.title: New Year surcharge
ground_rules.text: Ryokan: +50–100% on the normal per-person rate for 31 Dec–2 Jan, usually as a mandatory New Year plan with toshikoshi soba on the 31st and an osechi breakfast on 1 Jan (verified at Hakone Ginyu: +¥14,300 per person). City hotels: +30–80% on 31 Dec. Apartment hotels: roughly 1.5–2× the base rate.

ground_rules.title: Seven of us: four rooms, never one
ground_rules.text: Ryokan price per person. For three couples and Pedro's sister, ask for 3 rooms × 2 plus a single, or 2 rooms × 3 plus one room for a couple, the same plan and the same dinner sitting. Houses need three bedrooms and a sofa bed or a fourth room. One room for seven adults including a pregnant woman and two older parents is not advisable.

ground_rules.title: Beds, lifts, ground floors
ground_rules.text: Hotels always have lifts. Modern large ryokan do; small historic ones and machiya have steep stairs and bedrooms upstairs. Ask for a Japanese-Western room (和洋室): beds plus a tatami area. In a machiya, put her on the ground floor and check the bedrooms are heated.

ground_rules.title: Tell them she is pregnant
ground_rules.text: Say one guest is pregnant (妊娠中) and two are seniors: rooms near the lift, cooked courses instead of sashimi, low-sodium if needed, in-room dining if offered. Ryokan handle this routinely with three days' notice.

ground_rules.title: Refundable first
ground_rules.text: Hold city nights on official sites or Booking.com with free cancellation. Book the New Year ryokan on the strictest-but-still-refundable plan you can find (Ikyu and Rakuten show cancellation terms). Machiya brands charge in full at booking and refund to about 21–22 days out. Never hold more than two options per night.

ground_rules.title: The right channel
ground_rules.text: Hotels: official site or Booking.com. Ryokan: Ikyu (English, shows New Year plans), Rakuten Travel (about 10% cheaper than Booking), Jalan (Japanese only, most listings). A ryokan that shows sold out online often still has rooms by email for 2 rooms × 3. Machiya: the brand's own site.

ground_rules.title: Send the suitcases ahead
ground_rules.text: Yamato takkyubin hotel-to-hotel is about ¥2,000–2,800 per case, next day; allow an extra day from 28 Dec to 4 Jan. Travel the onsen nights with a daypack.

hotel.label: Hotel
hotel.blurb: Three rooms, or an apartment hotel with connecting units. A front desk for luggage forwarding and taxis.

rental.label: Whole house
rental.blurb: A machiya or apartment for six: a living room for the evenings, a kitchen and a washing machine. Usually beats three hotel rooms for three nights or more.

ryokan.label: Ryokan
ryokan.blurb: Dinner and breakfast included, a bath in the room. Priced per person. The nights where the stay itself is the point.

tokyo.why: Tokyo rentals are small and often far from stations. A front desk helps with luggage forwarding and taxis. Stay near a JR Yamanote line station; Asakusa, Ginza and Nihonbashi are calmer than Shinjuku over New Year.
tokyo.fit: Three double or twin rooms, two connecting apartments, or one 2–3 bedroom suite. Everything has lifts and beds.

candidates.name: MIMARU Tokyo Hatchobori
candidates.area: Hatchobori, between Tokyo Station and Ginza
candidates.what: 6-person Japanese apartment (two twins, a bunk and futon), or two connecting units with a door between them. Kitchen, washer.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift, kitchen; the best fit for three couples who want one door between them.

candidates.name: MIMARU SUITES Tokyo Asakusa
candidates.what: Two-bedroom suites for six with a living room and kitchen.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift. Senso-ji on the doorstep.

candidates.name: MIMARU SUITES Tokyo Nihombashi
candidates.what: Suites for 4–6 with kitchens, close to Tokyo Station for the 24 Dec shinkansen.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift.

candidates.name: Tokyu Stay Ginza
candidates.what: Rooms with a kitchenette and a washer-dryer, three rooms for six.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift, laundry in the room.

candidates.name: Oakwood Premier Tokyo
candidates.area: Marunouchi, on top of Tokyo Station
candidates.what: Serviced 1–2 bedroom apartments.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift, the station downstairs.

kanazawa.why: The longest stay. A shared living room for the evenings, a kitchen and a washing machine make it the mid-trip reset. Hotels are the fallback if the good machiya are gone.
kanazawa.fit: A machiya for exactly six with three bedrooms, or Hyatt House's kitchen rooms with connecting doors.
kanazawa.outlook: Open for hotels; tight for the nicest machiya. Omicho market closes 1–3 Jan, so our dates (24–28 Dec) are fine.

candidates.name: Machiya Residence Inn · Ainotsuji
candidates.what: A house for six: three bedrooms, two semi-double beds plus four futon, two bathrooms.
candidates.fit: Stairs; beds upstairs, futon can be laid downstairs for her. Paid in full at booking, refundable to 22 days.

candidates.name: Machiya Residence Inn · Hanatsume
candidates.what: Three bedrooms in the old samurai quarter.
candidates.fit: Stairs; ask for futon downstairs.

candidates.name: Hyatt House Kanazawa
candidates.what: 92 rooms, 78 with kitchens, connecting rooms, laundry.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift. The easy fallback.

candidates.name: Kanazawa Machiya Kenroku
candidates.what: A whole machiya for up to six; cheaper per person from two nights.
candidates.price: From ¥39,000 for two, rises with group size
candidates.fit: Stairs.

candidates.name: Dormy Inn or Tokyu Stay, three rooms
candidates.what: Business hotels with big public baths and free noodles at night.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift.

takayama.why: Two nights rarely justify a rental's cleaning fee. Walking distance to the market and the old town matters on icy streets.
takayama.fit: Three rooms at a small hotel in the old town, or a machiya for six if it is cheaper for the two nights.
takayama.outlook: Open to tight. Nohi buses to Shirakawa-go thin out 29 Dec–3 Jan; we arrive on the 28th.

candidates.name: The Machiya Hotel Takayama
candidates.what: 14 rooms, group-friendly, in a restored merchant house.
candidates.fit: Check for a lift; ask for ground-floor rooms.

candidates.name: Machiya Inns & Hotels · Takayama houses
candidates.what: Restored houses that sleep 6–8, from the group that runs about 80 houses in Kyoto, Kanazawa and Takayama.
candidates.fit: Stairs; futon downstairs for her.

candidates.name: Hidatei Hanaougi
candidates.what: Ryokan with private baths and kaiseki; New Year's Eve in the gentler alternative.
candidates.price: ¥250,000–400,000 with meals, two or three rooms
candidates.fit: Lift, Japanese-Western rooms on request.

candidates.name: Honjin Hiranoya Kachoan
candidates.what: Classic ryokan in the centre; the other candidate for a Takayama New Year's Eve.
candidates.fit: Lift; ask for beds.

gero.why: Restaurants close for New Year, so dinner and breakfast must be included. A flat town with footbaths, 45 minutes from Takayama and on the line to Kyoto.
gero.fit: Two rooms × 3 with the New Year plan: kaiseki on the 31st, osechi breakfast on 1 Jan. Ask for a room with its own bath, or book the private baths.
gero.outlook: Tight. New Year plans post on Jalan, Rakuten and Ikyu in September–October; the best-known houses clear within weeks. Book this month, and email if a site shows sold out.

candidates.name: Yunoshimakan
candidates.area: On the hill above the town, shuttle from the station
candidates.what: A 1931 wooden building (registered cultural property), four free private baths, dinner served in the room.
candidates.price: About ¥35,000–45,000 per person with meals, plus the New Year uplift
candidates.fit: Historic building with steps; ask for a room near the lift and dinner in the room.

candidates.name: Suimeikan
candidates.what: Large ryokan with three buildings, private baths to book, some rooms with their own onsen, Western-Japanese rooms.
candidates.price: About ¥30,000–45,000 per person with meals, plus the New Year uplift
candidates.fit: Lift, beds available, the easiest for the parents and her.

candidates.name: Bosenkan
candidates.what: Only about eight rooms have open-air baths and they sell out first.
candidates.fit: Ask for a bath-in-room pair of rooms.

kyoto.why: A house in Higashiyama for New Year's Eve: the Okera fire and the bells are a walk away, and buses and the subway do not run all night. A living room and a kitchen cover the days when most restaurants are closed. It also holds the big cases from about 26 Dec.
kyoto.fit: One townhouse for 7 with three bedrooms and beds on the ground floor for Fernanda, or a ryokan for 30–31 Dec with the New Year's Eve dinner plus a second base for 1–5 Jan (about a 10-minute taxi). Ask for the licence number.
kyoto.outlook: The hardest booking of the trip. Houses and apartment hotels were open in October; the famous machiya brands are tight; Nazuna's New Year dinner-plan rooms are gone. Prices are for six; ask again for seven.

candidates.name: Kyomachiya Miyabi Kiyomizu Bettei
candidates.what: A townhouse for up to 8, with 3 bedrooms.
candidates.fit: Ask about beds on the ground floor, heating and check-in on 30 Dec.

candidates.name: Villa Nene-no-michi “Kazeno Heritage”
candidates.what: The former HOTEL VMG Resort Kyoto: a whole villa or suites, a short walk from Kodai-ji's bell.
candidates.fit: Ask about beds and stairs.

candidates.name: Machiya Residence Inn · Hanatoki or Fujinoma
candidates.what: Houses for eight: two queens plus four futon. Outside Higashiyama, so a taxi home on New Year's Eve.
candidates.fit: Stairs.

candidates.name: MIMARU SUITES Kyoto Shijo
candidates.what: Apartment-hotel suites for 4–6 with kitchen and laundry; a front desk. Two suites for seven.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift. The easy fallback.

hakone.why: A ryokan with an open-air bath in each room, so all three couples get the same room and she controls the temperature and time. Kaiseki for dinner; ask for a cooked-only menu for her.
hakone.fit: Two rooms × 3, ideally Western or Japanese-Western rooms. Large modern houses have lifts.
hakone.outlook: Our dates (5–7 Jan) are after the New Year rush: tight at the top houses, open at the mid-size ones. 31 Dec would have been gone.

candidates.name: Gora Hanaougi
candidates.what: Open-air bath in every room; dinner and breakfast included.
candidates.price: About ¥45,000–55,000 per person with meals (half-board rooms for two about US$570–615)
candidates.fit: Lift, beds in some rooms; the first choice if we go to Hakone.

candidates.name: Kitanokaze Saryo
candidates.what: Open-air bath in every room, near the Pola and glass museums.
candidates.fit: Lift.

candidates.name: Hakone Ginyu
candidates.what: Private rotenburo on every terrace, Western rooms for 1–3, lobby on the top floor with a lift.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift. Email for two rooms.

candidates.name: Hakone Kowakien Ten-yu
candidates.what: Modern, large, Western-Japanese rooms, infinity bath.
candidates.fit: Lift, beds. The easiest fit for the parents.

candidates.name: Yoshiike Ryokan
candidates.what: Big garden, rooms up to six, lift.
candidates.fit: Lift.

candidates.name: Gora Kadan
candidates.what: A former imperial retreat, three Michelin Keys, open-air baths in the suites.
candidates.fit: Lift.

kinosaki.why: The town is the baths; a ryokan gives the yukata, the bath pass and the crab kaiseki. Choose one with a private bath for her because the public ones run hot.
kinosaki.fit: Two or three rooms; the Nishimuraya houses have Western beds and lifts.
kinosaki.outlook: Tight. Crab season plus New Year is Kinosaki's peak and two-night plans are common; our dates (5–7 Jan) are just after the rush.

candidates.name: Nishimuraya Hotel Shogetsutei
candidates.what: 98 rooms, Western and Western-Japanese rooms, lift, crab kaiseki; a ¥2,000 per room voucher for direct booking.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift.

candidates.name: Nishimuraya Honkan
candidates.what: 1860, Relais & Châteaux, snow-crab kaiseki.
candidates.fit: Historic; stairs in parts.

candidates.name: Morizuya, Tsutaya or Mikuniya
candidates.what: Mid-size family inns on the canal.
candidates.fit: Stairs in most.

yudanaka.why: Christmas Eve at a ryokan, with dinner served, then Shibu's lantern lane; the snow monkeys the next morning.
yudanaka.fit: Rooms for 7 with beds and a private or in-room bath; a lift. Small historic inns have stairs and futons, so ask before booking.
yudanaka.outlook: For 24–26 Dec, not checked yet. The New Year nights are sold out at the small inns, but before Christmas should be easier. Prices are for six; ask again for seven.

candidates.name: Kokuya
candidates.what: Ryokan on the Shibu lane with private baths.
candidates.price: ¥150,000–240,000 for six with meals (to check for seven)
candidates.fit: Private baths, lift.

candidates.name: Kanaguya
candidates.what: A four-storey wooden ryokan on the lantern lane, with rooms for 6. Its own site warns of fake emails, so book only there.
candidates.fit: Historic building: ask about stairs, beds and a private bath.

candidates.name: Biyunoyado
candidates.what: Large modern ryokan with a lift, Japanese-Western rooms and a shuttle to the monkey park.
candidates.price: ¥150,000–240,000 for six with meals (to check for seven)
candidates.fit: Beds, lift.

okuhida.why: The snow baths are the point; dinner is at the inn because there is nothing else.
okuhida.fit: Two rooms at an inn with a lift and an open-air bath.

candidates.name: Hirayu or Shinhotaka inns
candidates.what: Rotenburo in the snow; the official association lists the inns.
candidates.fit: Check for a lift.

okayama.why: A station hotel for two nights makes Himeji, Kurashiki and the Naoshima ferry easy.

candidates.name: Hotel Granvia Okayama
candidates.what: The station hotel.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift.

candidates.name: Benesse House Park, Naoshima
candidates.what: The art hotel's lift wing; museum closures around New Year to check.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift.

hiroshima.why: Two nights near the station or the Peace Park.

candidates.name: Sheraton Grand or Hotel Granvia Hiroshima
candidates.what: Station hotels for a short stay.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift.

kawaguchiko.why: The lake is the point: a room on the north or east shore that looks straight at Fuji, so the first light on the mountain happens from bed. A lake hotel with beds and a lift suits the parents and her; the hoto houses cover lunch, and dinner is at the hotel or in town.
kawaguchiko.fit: Three rooms for two at a lakeside hotel with beds and a lift, Fuji-side rooms asked for by name. Konansou's lake-view rooms take up to six but are tatami only, so only with its Western-Japanese wing.
kawaguchiko.outlook: Our dates (5–7 Jan) are after the first-sunrise rush: open at the hotels, tight at Konansou and the top houses. 31 Dec would have been gone.

candidates.name: Fujikawaguchiko Onsen Ubuya
candidates.what: Every room faces the lake and Fuji; in-room open-air baths in the better rooms; kaiseki dinner.
candidates.fit: Lift, Western-Japanese rooms with beds. The first one to ask, for the Fuji view from the room; not yet checked on an official site.

candidates.name: Fuji View Hotel
candidates.what: The classic 1936 lakeside hotel: Western beds, a garden on the water, restaurants.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift. The easiest fit for the parents.

candidates.name: Hotel Mystays Fuji Onsen Resort
candidates.what: Modern, beds, lift, onsen with a Fuji view.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift.

candidates.name: Konansou
candidates.what: Tamayura lake-view rooms for 1–6, lift, rooftop foot bath with the Fuji view; half-board.
candidates.price: From ¥70,400 for two half-board; about ¥200,000 for six in normal season
candidates.fit: Lift; tatami only, so ask for the Western-Japanese wing or a bed. Verified on Ikyu.

candidates.name: Fufu Kawaguchiko
candidates.what: All-suite, beds, an onsen in every room.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift, in-room onsen for her.

candidates.name: Hoshinoya Fuji
candidates.what: Glamping cabins facing Fuji, beds, outdoor fires; three cabins for six.
candidates.fit: Beds; a buggy up the hill; New Year plans usually two-night minimum.

miyajima.why: The reason to sleep on the island is the evening, after the crowds have gone. On 31 Dec the restaurants close and the inn is where dinner happens. Book a ryokan with dinner and breakfast as one plan for all seven.
miyajima.fit: Two or three rooms: a large Japanese-Western room for four to six, plus a twin. Ask for beds for Fernanda, Carlos and Nadir, and a room near the lift.
miyajima.outlook: Tight for 30 Dec–1 Jan. The island has few large inns and the New Year plans go early. Easy before Christmas. If the island is full, sleep in Hiroshima and come over on the 30th or 31st.

candidates.name: Miyajima Grand Hotel Arimoto
candidates.what: Calls itself the island's oldest inn, over 400 years old. Japanese-Western rooms of up to 99 m², with two beds and futons for six.
candidates.price: About ¥130,000–180,000 for six with meals; 50–100% more for 30–31 Dec
candidates.fit: Beds in the Japanese-Western rooms. Booking sites list a lift; confirm it.

candidates.name: Itsukushima Iroha
candidates.what: Fifteen rooms of about 50 m² for up to four, some with twin beds, and a rooftop bath that looks across the water to the torii.
candidates.price: From about ¥50,000 per person with dinner and breakfast, so roughly ¥300,000 for six
candidates.fit: Twin beds, lift.

candidates.name: Iwaso
candidates.area: Momijidani, about 300 m behind the shrine
candidates.what: Founded in 1854 and one of the few inns on the island with its own hot spring. There is a main building, a new building and cottages; a corner room in the new building takes two to six.
candidates.price: From about ¥25,000 per person without meals; with kaiseki, roughly ¥250,000–380,000 for six
candidates.fit: Japanese rooms with futons. There are lifts, and the new building is step-free from the entrance.

shirahama.why: Shirahama's big onsen hotels sell half board, and over New Year, when the town's restaurants close, the hotel dinner is the easy answer. Choose one with a lift, beds and a private or in-room bath for Fernanda.
shirahama.fit: Three rooms or suites for two, plus a single, or two Japanese-style rooms for three or four.
shirahama.outlook: Tight for 30 Dec–1 Jan, because the coast is a favourite Kansai New Year escape. Open before Christmas and after 4 Jan.

candidates.name: Hotel Kawakyu
candidates.what: A grand palace-style hotel where every room is a suite of 66–70 m² for two or three. Dinner is a buffet, and a few suites have their own open-air bath.
candidates.price: From about ¥50,000 for two with dinner and breakfast, so roughly ¥150,000–250,000 for six; more at New Year
candidates.fit: Twin beds in every suite.

candidates.name: Shirahama Coganoi Resort & Spa
candidates.area: Above the sea; free shuttle from JR Shirahama
candidates.what: Kaiseki at its restaurant, with a lighter-portion course. Sea-view rooms with balconies, including a two-room Japanese suite (10 + 6 tatami), and an open-air bath above a wide pool of water.
candidates.fit: Twin rooms and Japanese rooms; ask for beds.

candidates.name: Nanki-Shirahama Marriott Hotel
candidates.what: Japanese-style rooms of 42 m² for up to four, with garden or sea views; some rooms have an onsen bath. Dinner plans in the restaurant.
candidates.price: From about ¥21,000–26,000 a room without meals; roughly ¥110,000–160,000 for six with dinner
candidates.fit: Beds in the twin rooms; ask about the Japanese rooms.

nagano.why: Nagano is a base for day trips, so a hotel by the station makes sense. Trains to the monkeys, Matsumoto and the ski villages leave from the door, and taxis wait outside.
nagano.fit: Three or four rooms: a twin for each couple and a single for Tatiana. Everything has lifts and beds.
nagano.outlook: Open before Christmas. The ski weeks and New Year fill sooner.

candidates.name: Hotel Metropolitan Nagano
candidates.what: A JR hotel with twin rooms of about 25 m², several restaurants and a bar, and the shinkansen downstairs.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift, and no walking on ice to the train.

candidates.name: Dormy Inn Nagano
candidates.area: A few minutes' walk from the station
candidates.what: A business hotel with a natural hot-spring bath on the top floor, including an open-air pool, and free late-night ramen.
candidates.fit: Small rooms, lift. The shared bath is for the others; Fernanda has her room's bathroom.

candidates.name: Fuchinobo
candidates.what: One of the 39 temple lodgings at Zenko-ji, with lockable rooms (one has three tatami bedrooms and a sitting room) and the dawn service a short walk away.
candidates.price: Priced per person; ask by email
candidates.fit: Futons, and shared baths in the basement. One night for the experience, not for Fernanda.

arima.why: Arima is a ryokan town: the inn's own baths, dinner and breakfast are the stay. Book one with private baths so Fernanda can soak briefly at a temperature she likes; the gold water runs hot.
arima.fit: Two or three rooms. Arima Grand Hotel has a Japanese-Western room for six with two beds and four futons, plus a twin for the seventh.
arima.outlook: The large houses should have room after 2 Jan. New Year nights (31 Dec–2 Jan) come with special plans and prices, and the small, famous inns go early.

candidates.name: Hyoe Koyokaku
candidates.area: Centre of town, five minutes' walk from the bus terminal
candidates.what: A large inn with 126 rooms and some 700 years of history. Nine baths of gold and silver water, plus two private open-air baths to book (¥3,200–4,200 for 50 minutes). A corner suite opened in 2024.
candidates.price: ¥25,900–109,000 per person with meals, so about ¥160,000–300,000 for six
candidates.fit: Mostly Japanese rooms; ask for beds and a room near the lift.

candidates.name: Arima Grand Hotel
candidates.what: Japanese-Western rooms for six (two beds and four futons, about 87 m²), private baths and a private spa, and kaiseki plans with Kobe beef.
candidates.fit: Two beds in each family room; lift.

candidates.name: Taketoritei Maruyama
candidates.area: Quiet edge of town, short shuttle from the bus terminal
candidates.what: Thirty rooms, five with open-air baths and eight with indoor baths, and eight private baths free for 45 minutes.
candidates.price: ¥62,200–171,000 per person with meals, so ¥380,000 or more for six
candidates.fit: A small luxury inn; ask about stairs and beds.

osaka.why: Osaka copes with New Year better than Kyoto: the chain restaurants and Dotonbori stay open, and the food halls are back from the 2nd. An apartment hotel in Namba puts Dotonbori, Kuromon and the Kintetsu line to Nara on the doorstep, with a kitchen and a washer for a long stay.
osaka.fit: One three-bedroom suite for six plus a room for Tatiana, or two triples and a single. Everything has lifts and beds.
osaka.outlook: Open at all tiers. New Year's Eve and the USJ countdown push Namba prices up on the 31st.

candidates.name: MIMARU Osaka Namba Station Annex
candidates.what: The Sky Garden suite: 100 m², three bedrooms with six single beds, a bath and a shower room, two toilets, a kitchen and a washer-dryer. Six minutes to the Kintetsu line for Nara.
candidates.price: About ¥70,000–120,000 for the suite, plus a room for the seventh
candidates.fit: Beds, lift, kitchen. Book a second, smaller unit for Tatiana.

candidates.name: Cross Hotel Osaka
candidates.what: A design hotel with triple rooms of about 27 m² (three beds side by side) and a tub in each bathroom.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift. Two triples and a single cover all seven.

nara.why: For more than one night, a house gives a kitchen and a table for seven while restaurants close on 1–3 Jan, and puts you in the park before the day visitors arrive. For a single night, a hotel by the park is simpler.
nara.fit: A house with three or four bedrooms and beds; check there is a ground-floor bedroom for Fernanda. Nara has few houses this size, so the fallback is three rooms at a hotel.
nara.outlook: Few large houses, so book early for New Year. Hotels have room; the business hotels near the stations are the fallback.

candidates.name: KONJAKUSO Nara Kitamachi "MANAKA"
candidates.area: Kitamachi, near Todai-ji; 10 minutes' walk from Kintetsu Nara
candidates.what: A whole house of 188 m² with four bedrooms and eight beds, an open-air Shigaraki-ware tub in the courtyard, and a washer-dryer.
candidates.price: From about ¥111,600 a night for two without meals; expect ¥180,000–300,000 for six
candidates.fit: Beds; not step-free, so check where the bedrooms are.

candidates.name: Nara Hotel
candidates.area: On the edge of Nara Park
candidates.what: A 1909 hotel by Kingo Tatsuno in cypress wood. The West building was renewed in 2026.
candidates.fit: Beds. Ask for the West building if the lift matters.

candidates.name: Hotel Fujita Nara
candidates.area: Sanjo-dori, five minutes from JR Nara
candidates.what: A plain business hotel on the main street to the park, with twins that take an extra bed and a few triples.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift.

kamakura.why: Kamakura is small and goes to bed early, so a hotel with a restaurant matters more than a kitchen. By the sea at Shichirigahama you see Fuji at sunset on clear days; by the station you are closer to the temples. Either way Haneda is about an hour.
kamakura.fit: Three twins and a single. Everything has lifts and beds.
kamakura.outlook: Open for 5–9 Jan, once the New Year crowds have gone. Avoid 1–3 Jan.

candidates.name: Kamakura Prince Hotel
candidates.area: Shichirigahama, on the hill above the beach
candidates.what: 97 rooms, all facing the sea; from the third and fourth floors you look to Enoshima and Fuji. French and Japanese restaurants, and a short walk to the Enoden.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift.

candidates.name: Hotel Metropolitan Kamakura
candidates.area: Two minutes from JR Kamakura's east exit
candidates.what: A modern hotel in Komachi, among the shops near the station.
candidates.price: Plans from about ¥22,000 a room, so roughly ¥60,000–100,000 for three
candidates.fit: Beds, lift; the station is on the doorstep for the airport.

matsue.why: With restaurants shut over New Year, a lakeside onsen inn makes it easy: dinner and breakfast included, osechi on 1 Jan, and Lake Shinji outside the window. Choose a room with its own bath for Fernanda.
matsue.fit: Three rooms and a single, or two rooms for three and one for a couple. Naniwa Issui and Minamikan have rooms with private baths; Hotel Ichibata has lake-side triples, beds and a lift.
matsue.outlook: Probably open. Matsue is far quieter over New Year than the famous onsen towns, but the few rooms with their own baths go first. Check 31 Dec in a browser.

candidates.name: Hotel Ichibata
candidates.what: 132 rooms, with lake-side triples of 36 m² and a top-floor onsen looking over the lake; a minute from the Ichibata line station.
candidates.price: Lake-side triples from about ¥18,000 a room without meals; about ¥130,000–200,000 for six with dinner over New Year (estimate)
candidates.fit: Beds, lift. No private baths: Fernanda would use the shared bath at quiet hours or the room's tub.

candidates.name: Naniwa Issui
candidates.what: 25 rooms facing the lake; seven with their own open-air hot-spring bath, plus four designer Minamo rooms with baths; kaiseki of lake fish.
candidates.price: ¥25,700–62,200 per person with dinner and breakfast, so about ¥155,000–375,000 for six; New Year plans cost more
candidates.fit: Ask for the rooms with private baths, and beds where they have them.

candidates.name: Minamikan
candidates.area: By the lake, five minutes' walk from the castle
candidates.what: A garden inn of 19 rooms, some with a bath looking over Lake Shinji; known for its sea-bream rice.
candidates.price: Not published; expect ¥350,000 or more for six with meals over New Year (estimate)
candidates.fit: Small and traditional; ask about beds and stairs.

fukuoka.why: Over 1–3 Jan most stalls and many restaurants are shut, so a kitchen and a living room help. An apartment near Hakata or Tenjin also puts the yatai a short walk away once they reopen. Three hotel rooms and a single are the easy fallback.
fukuoka.fit: An apartment for six to eight with a fourth bed or sofa bed, or three rooms and a single at a station hotel.
fukuoka.outlook: Open. Fukuoka is quiet over New Year and city prices barely move; the new Richmond family rooms may go quickly.

candidates.name: HOTEL All Stay Hakata Kukodori
candidates.what: Seven apartments with kitchenettes and washer-dryers, the largest 71 m² for up to eleven; contactless check-in.
candidates.fit: Everyone in one unit. No front desk, so no luggage forwarding from the door.

candidates.name: Richmond Hotel Fukuoka Tenjin
candidates.area: Tenjin, three minutes from Tenjin-Minami station
candidates.what: Closed for a full refit and due to reopen on 24 Dec 2026, reportedly with new 48 m² family rooms for up to six (four beds, two of them sofa beds).
candidates.price: Not yet published; Richmond rates are usually modest (estimate ¥50,000–80,000 for six)
candidates.fit: Beds, lift, front desk. Brand new, but confirm the family rooms exist before counting on them.

candidates.name: Hotel Nikko Fukuoka
candidates.area: Three minutes from Hakata station by underground passage
candidates.what: A large, well-run hotel; twins of 29–35 m² from about ¥27,000 a room.
candidates.price: About ¥90,000–120,000 for three twins and a single
candidates.fit: Beds, lift, a front desk for taxis and bags, and under cover all the way to the shinkansen.

nagoya.why: One or two nights on the way through, so a hotel on top of the station: no taxis with bags, and the train out is a lift ride away.
nagoya.fit: Three rooms and a single, or a corner room for three and two twins. GRAND BASE has apartments that sleep seven.
nagoya.outlook: Open. Nagoya is a business city and quiet in the first week of January.

candidates.name: Nagoya JR Gate Tower Hotel
candidates.what: 350 rooms on floors 15–24; doubles from about ¥27,500 and 28 m² twins from about ¥33,000 a room. Some rooms look down on the shinkansen tracks.
candidates.price: About ¥100,000–130,000 for three twins and a single
candidates.fit: Beds, lift, under one roof with the trains. Maglev construction may be audible in some rooms.

candidates.name: Nagoya Marriott Associa Hotel
candidates.area: JR Central Towers, above the station
candidates.what: Rooms on floors 20–49 and a 54 m² family room for four.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift, and the view.

candidates.name: GRAND BASE Nagoya Ekinishi
candidates.area: West side, about ten minutes' walk from the station
candidates.what: Apartments with kitchens and washing machines; a 40 m² unit for seven and larger three-bedroom units.
candidates.fit: Everyone together; take a taxi from the station with the bags.

atami.why: For a few nights by the sea, a resort hotel with Japanese-Western family rooms is simpler and cheaper than a ryokan, and dinner can be in town or at the hotel.
atami.fit: One large Japanese-Western room for six or seven plus a single, or two family rooms.
atami.outlook: Open for the days before New Year; the bay hotels fill for the 25 Dec fireworks, and 31 Dec–2 Jan is tight and dear.

candidates.name: KKR Hotel Atami
candidates.what: A public servants' mutual-aid hotel that also takes the public; a 46 m² Japanese-Western room with a bedroom and six tatami, listed for up to seven.
candidates.fit: Beds and futon in one room, lift. Check that non-members can book these dates.

candidates.name: Hotel Sunmi Club
candidates.area: Wadahama, ten minutes by car south of the station
candidates.what: 47 m² Japanese rooms (ten tatami plus six) for up to six, or Japanese-Western rooms with twin beds for up to five; sea-view open-air baths.
candidates.price: Rooms from about ¥17,000–25,000 for two; about ¥90,000–130,000 for six with breakfast (estimate)
candidates.fit: Lift. No private baths, so the shared baths at quiet hours.

candidates.name: RISONARE Atami
candidates.area: Hillside above the town, free shuttle 15 minutes from the station
candidates.what: Hoshino Resorts' family hotel: 81 rooms, all over 60 m², some for up to six; a seafood buffet or kaiseki with kinmedai. A desk by the station sends bags up.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift and room to spread out.

ise-shima.why: The bay-view hotels in Toba have Japanese-Western rooms for families, restaurants that keep going over New Year, and the station a short shuttle away.
ise-shima.fit: Two rooms for three and one for a couple, or a tatami room for five and a twin.
ise-shima.outlook: Probably open from 1 Jan; the New Year nights themselves are dear, and the Kintetsu seats can sell out before the rooms do.

candidates.name: Toba Grand Hotel
candidates.area: Kohama, five minutes by car from Toba station, with a shuttle
candidates.what: Sea-view baths, 12-tatami ocean-view rooms for five on the top floor, and dinners with Ise lobster in the room or at a buffet.
candidates.fit: Lift; mostly tatami and futon.

candidates.name: Toba Hotel International
candidates.area: On the hill above Toba Bay, near the station
candidates.what: Ocean Wing and Harbour Wing rooms and suites, some Japanese-Western for up to five; French and Japanese restaurants.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift. Some rooms face the hill, so ask for the bay.

candidates.name: Shima Kanko Hotel The Classic
candidates.area: Kashikojima, 40 minutes south of Toba by Kintetsu
candidates.what: The grand old hotel over Ago Bay, known for its French cooking with Ise lobster and abalone; The Bay Suites next door.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift; the rooms are for two, so four rooms.

morioka.why: A city base for day trips by shinkansen: a hotel joined to the station keeps the cold morning starts short and off the ice.
morioka.fit: Three rooms and a single, or two triples and a twin.
morioka.outlook: Open. Morioka is quiet and cheap in December and the city hotels do not sell out.

candidates.name: Hotel Metropolitan Morioka (main building)
candidates.area: Joined to Morioka station through the Fesan building
candidates.what: 190 rooms, some renovated in 2025; the station is a minute away indoors.
candidates.price: About ¥45,000–70,000 for three twins and a single (estimate)
candidates.fit: Beds, lift, and no ice between the room and the trains.

candidates.name: Hotel Metropolitan Morioka New Wing
candidates.area: Three minutes' walk from the station
candidates.what: The newer, larger wing, with triples of about 30 m²: two beds and a sofa bed.
candidates.price: About ¥60,000–90,000 for two triples and a twin (estimate)
candidates.fit: Beds, lift.

tsunagi.why: The village is the hotels: dinner, breakfast and the bath are the stay. A room with its own open-air bath means Fernanda never crosses ice to reach one.
tsunagi.fit: Two or three rooms; ask for lake-side rooms with private baths, and beds where they have them.
tsunagi.outlook: Uncertain for 31 Dec: New Year is the busiest time of the year here, and Taikan's eleven rooms with baths go first.

candidates.name: Hotel Shion
candidates.what: Lake-side tatami rooms for up to five, twins on the fourth floor, and 63 m² top-floor rooms for up to six; a lakeside rock bath.
candidates.price: From about ¥12,000 per person with dinner and breakfast on an early-booking plan; about ¥110,000–160,000 for six over New Year (estimate)
candidates.fit: Lift. Some premium rooms have their own bath, so ask.

candidates.name: Nanbu Yumori-no-yado Taikan
candidates.what: 120 rooms, eleven with their own open-air bath; a shuttle from Morioka station by booking.
candidates.price: ¥9,000–88,500 per person with dinner and breakfast; about ¥160,000–250,000 for six in rooms with baths over New Year (estimate)
candidates.fit: Lift; a big hotel with a buffet or kaiseki.

candidates.name: Bessou Kakei
candidates.area: Tsunagi, set apart from the big hotels
candidates.what: Six villa suites of 100 m², each with an open-air rock bath and an indoor bath with a view, for up to three.
candidates.price: From about ¥43,000 per person with dinner and breakfast; about ¥300,000–450,000 for three villas over New Year (estimate)
candidates.fit: Private and quiet; ask about beds and steps.

south-tohoku.why: A city base for day trips: a hotel by the station keeps Matsushima's train and the shinkansen a short walk away.
south-tohoku.fit: Two four-bed family rooms at The Base, or three rooms and a single.
south-tohoku.outlook: Open. Sendai has plenty of rooms in December; the Pageant weekends are the busiest.

candidates.name: Hotel Metropolitan The Base Sendai
candidates.area: Two minutes from the station's west exit
candidates.what: Opened in April 2026: 56 rooms, including four-bed family rooms (flat beds or bunks) with a microwave, fridge and tableware.
candidates.price: Twins from about ¥12,000; about ¥40,000–65,000 for two four-bed rooms (estimate)
candidates.fit: Beds, lift; two family rooms sleep all seven. Ask for flat beds, not bunks, for Fernanda and the parents.

candidates.name: Hotel Metropolitan Sendai East
candidates.what: 282 rooms, with superior triples of 34 m².
candidates.price: About ¥60,000–90,000 for two triples and a single (estimate)
candidates.fit: Beds, lift.

candidates.name: The Westin Sendai
candidates.area: Ichibancho, ten minutes' walk or one subway stop from the station
candidates.what: Rooms averaging about 43 m² on floors 28–36, high over the city.
candidates.fit: Beds, lift, big bathrooms.

north-tohoku.why: A city hotel near Aomori station keeps the snowy walks short and the trains to Hirosaki and Shin-Aomori close, with restaurants and food halls nearby once the town reopens after 1 Jan.
north-tohoku.fit: Three rooms and a single, or the Yasukata villa suite for all seven.
north-tohoku.outlook: Open. Aomori is cheap, and New Year barely moves the prices.

candidates.name: Tsunageru Aomori Yasukata VillaSuite
candidates.area: Yasukata, about ten minutes' walk from Aomori station
candidates.what: An 89 m² suite with three bedrooms and a big living room for up to nine, renovated in 2023, with self-catering; also 50 m² Japanese-Western rooms for five.
candidates.price: From about ¥28,000 a night for the suite, room only
candidates.fit: All seven together with a kitchen; take a taxi in the snow.

candidates.name: Hotel JAL City Aomori
candidates.area: Six minutes' walk from Aomori station, by the bay
candidates.what: 167 rooms, some facing the bay and the Bay Bridge, partly renovated in 2025 with Tsugaru kogin stitching.
candidates.price: About ¥45,000–75,000 for three twins and a single (estimate)
candidates.fit: Beds, lift, a front desk.

shuzenji.why: Shuzenji is an onsen town where the inn is the evening: dinner, breakfast and a bath. Over New Year, with little open in the village, dinner at the inn every night is the simple answer. Choose a room with its own bath for Fernanda.
shuzenji.fit: Two or three rooms at one inn, at least one with beds and a private bath. Arai has a 116 m² river-view room for six.
shuzenji.outlook: Tight for 31 Dec–2 Jan: the small inns load New Year plans early and the rooms with baths go first. 28–30 Dec is easier.

candidates.name: Breezbay Shuzenji Hotel
candidates.area: Hillside, ten minutes by car from Shuzenji station
candidates.what: Japanese-Western rooms with twin beds and tatami for up to four; a private bath to book and a large public bath.
candidates.price: From about ¥12,000 a room without meals; about ¥110,000–170,000 for six with dinner over New Year (estimate)
candidates.fit: Beds. Outside the village, so taxis for the bamboo path.

candidates.name: Tofuya Resort & Spa-Izu
candidates.what: 30 rooms, 23 with their own open-air hot-spring bath, in Japanese, Japanese-Western and Western styles.
candidates.price: ¥30,800–78,200 per person with dinner and breakfast; about ¥190,000–320,000 for six in the standard rooms, more over New Year
candidates.fit: Ask for Japanese-Western rooms with beds and a bath.

candidates.name: Arai Ryokan
candidates.area: On the river in the village centre
candidates.what: An inn from 1872 whose wooden buildings are listed cultural properties; a 116 m² river-view room for six, renovated in 2023.
candidates.price: About ¥350,000–550,000 for six with meals over New Year (estimate)
candidates.fit: Historic: tatami and futon, stairs in parts.
